events.title: Henry II is crowned king of England at Westminster Abbey
events.description: Henry II, the first Plantagenet king, was crowned in Westminster Abbey. His lands in England, Normandy, Anjou and, through his wife Eleanor, Aquitaine were later called the Angevin Empire.
events.html: Henry II, the first Plantagenet king, was crowned in Westminster Abbey. His lands in England, Normandy, Anjou and, through his wife Eleanor, Aquitaine were later called the Angevin Empire.

events.title: Paolo Scolari is elected pope as Clement III
events.description: Paolo Scolari was elected pope as Clement III. He ended the conflict between the papacy and the city of Rome by allowing the election of magistrates, which brought the papacy back to the city after a six-year exile.
events.html: Paolo Scolari was elected pope as Clement III. He ended the conflict between the papacy and the city of Rome by allowing the election of magistrates, which brought the papacy back to the city after a six-year exile.

events.title: Anne of Brittany marries Maximilian I by proxy
events.description: Anne, Duchess of Brittany since 1488, was married by proxy to Maximilian I, King of the Romans. She went on to marry Charles VIII of France in 1491 and Louis XII in 1499, twice becoming queen of France.
events.html: Anne, Duchess of Brittany since 1488, was married by proxy to Maximilian I, King of the Romans. She went on to marry Charles VIII of France in 1491 and Louis XII in 1499, twice becoming queen of France.

events.title: Catholics and Huguenots clash at Dreux
events.description: The first major battle of the French Wars of Religion was fought at Dreux, west of Paris. Both armies' commanders were captured, and the bloody outcome showed the war would be long.
events.html: The first major battle of the French Wars of Religion was fought at Dreux, west of Paris. Both armies' commanders were captured, and the bloody outcome showed the war would be long.

events.title: New England militia defeat the Narragansett in the Great Swamp Fight
events.description: In King Philip's War, New England colonial militia, with 150 Pequot allies, defeated the Narragansett people near Kingston, Rhode Island, inflicting a huge number of casualties, including many hundreds of women and children. It is also called the Great Swamp Massacre.

events.title: Thomas Paine publishes the first pamphlet of The American Crisis
events.description: The first pamphlet of Thomas Paine's series The American Crisis appeared in The Pennsylvania Journal, signed "Common Sense". The series ran to thirteen numbered pamphlets by 1777 and three more by 1783, during the American Revolution.
events.html: The first pamphlet of Thomas Paine's series The American Crisis appeared in The Pennsylvania Journal, signed "Common Sense". The series ran to thirteen numbered pamphlets by 1777 and three more by 1783, during the American Revolution.

events.title: Washington's army goes into winter quarters at Valley Forge
events.description: About 12,000 Continental soldiers marched into camp at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania. Some 2,000 died of disease over the winter, but drilling under Baron von Steuben made the survivors a more effective army.
events.html: About 12,000 Continental soldiers marched into camp at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania. Some 2,000 died of disease over the winter, but drilling under Baron von Steuben made the survivors a more effective army.

events.title: The Siege of Toulon ends as the British abandon the city
events.description: French artillery under Napoleon Bonaparte forced the British to abandon Toulon, ending the Republic's siege of the port, held by Royalists aided by the First Coalition. The recapture secured southern France from invasion.
events.html: French artillery under Napoleon Bonaparte forced the British to abandon Toulon, ending the Republic's siege of the port, held by Royalists aided by the First Coalition. The recapture secured southern France from invasion.

events.title: Charles Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol
events.description: Charles Dickens's novella about the miser Ebenezer Scrooge went on sale and sold out its first printing by Christmas Eve. It shaped Victorian ideals of a charitable, family-centred Christmas.

events.title: The House impeaches President Clinton
events.description: The US House of Representatives impeached Bill Clinton for perjury and obstruction of justice related to the Monica Lewinsky affair. The Senate acquitted him in February 1999.
